chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Nuh ibn Shu'ayb and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, who said:
Ibn Abi al-Awjah asked Hisham ibn al-Hakam, so he said to him, 'Is Allah not All-Wise?' He said, 'Yes, and He is the most Wise of the wise.'

He said, 'So inform me about His Words, the Mighty and Majestic: "Then marry such women as seem good to you, two and three and four; but if you fear that you will not do justice (between them), then (marry) only one." Is this not an obligation?' He said, 'Yes.'

He said, 'So inform me about His Words, the Mighty and Majestic: "And you have it not in your power to do justice between wives, even though you may wish (it), but be not disinclined (from one) with total disinclination." Which Wise One would speak with this?'
So there did not happen to be an answer with him. So he traveled to Medina to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him).
So he said, 'O Hisham! (You have come) at such a time which is neither of Hajj nor of Umrah?' He said, 'Yes, May I be sacrificed for you.'
It has concerned me that Ibn Abi al-Awjah asked me a question for which there was no answer with me with regards to it.' He said, 'And what is it?'
He said, 'So I informed him of the story.'

So Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'As for His Words, the Mighty and Majestic: "Then marry such women as seem good to you, two and three and four; but if you fear that you will not do justice (between them), then (marry) only one," meaning regarding the expenditure.'

And as for His Words: "And you have it not in your power to do justice between wives, even though you may wish (it), but be not disinclined (from one) with total disinclination, so that you leave her as it were in suspense," so it is regarding the cordiality.'
He (the narrator) said, 'So when Hisham proceeded to him with the answer and informed him, he said, 'By Allah! This is not from yourself'.

key_terms.أَحْكَمُ الْحَاكِمِينَ: The most Wise of the judges

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the justice required for multiple wives in Quran 4:3 and the justice mentioned in Quran 4:129?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the scholarly debate between Hisham ibn al-Hakam and Ibn Abi al-Auja regarding the scope of justice in polygamy, resolved by Imam al-Sadiq (AS). The Imam distinguishes between material equity (nafaqah), which is obligatory, and emotional affection (mawaddah), which is naturally variable and not strictly required to be equal. This distinction preserves the validity of marrying up to four wives despite the Quranic admission that perfect emotional balance is unattainable.
